message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) belong to very different mammalian lineages—Carnivora for the lion and Perissodactyla for the zebra.  
Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which contains both Carnivora and Perissodactyla. This ancestor was a placental mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, long before the diversification of modern cats and horses.
